t: Minimum Operations to Transform Array into Alternating Prime
o: Even indices must hold primes, odd indices non-primes; each operation increments one element by 1, so the cost for a slot is the distance to the nearest qualifying value at or above it. Precompute primality with a sieve up to slightly above 1e5 (the next prime after 100000 is 100003) and a next-prime table.
k: Only increments are allowed, so cost at even index v is nextPrime(v) - v; at odd index it is 0 if v is composite/non-prime, else 1 or 2 (to v+1 or v+2).
A sieve to 100004 covers all cases since 100003 is prime and 100001, 100002 are composite.

a.i: Sieve booleans, then fill nxt[v] = smallest prime >= v by a backward scan. Even slots add nxt[v]-v; odd slots add 0 if not prime, else 1 if v+1 is composite else 2.
a.t: O(LIM log log LIM + n) — sieve plus linear pass

w: Slots are independent, so the answer is just the sum of per-slot minimal increments. Pitfall: sieving only to 1e5 (you need 100003), and treating 1 as prime (it is not). Note 1 is non-prime, so an odd slot holding 1 costs 0. Follow-up: allow decrements too (then cost is distance to the nearest qualifying value on either side), or alternating prime/composite patterns of period k.
